_note: v2 'The Week Wall Street Broke' (16:9). [text, pause after (s)]. Numbers spelled out for the voice.

a_hook: A one hundred fifty-eight year old bank just died overnight.
And it was only the beginning.
b_houses: To understand why, go back a few years.
America was obsessed with one thing:
c_subprime: Banks were handing out mortgages to almost anyone.
d_mbs: But the banks didn't keep them.
They bundled thousands together into products called mortgage-backed securities.
Rating agencies stamped them triple-A, the safest grade there is.
And they were sold to pension funds, banks and governments around the world.
e_leverage: To buy more, Wall Street borrowed.
Lehman Brothers was betting thirty dollars for every one it actually had.
f_fall: Those triple-A bundles were suddenly worth almost nothing.
And nobody knew who was holding them.
g_panic: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, seized by the government.
h_weekend: America's top bankers, locked inside the New York Fed.
i_bankrupt: Monday morning, Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy.
Six hundred and thirty-nine billion dollars.
j_contagion: The next day, A.I.G. needed eighty-five billion just to survive.
Banks stopped lending to each other.
k_cost: Nearly nine million Americans lost their jobs.
Governments spent trillions to stop the whole system from collapsing.
l_end: And all of it was built on one assumption:
that house prices would never fall.
